results.text: DHL.mono: DHL[k,2] implies DHL[k',2] for every k' ≥ k (delete shifts), with Admissible.sublist.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Proposition 12: M_{k,eps} ≤ (1+eps) M_k, and M_{k,eps} ≥ (1+eps) M_k − 64k²eps²/M_k for small eps, so the enlargement gains exactly (1+eps) to first order. Possibly folklore.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Theorem 13 (floor of the epsilon-enlarged simplex): M_{k,eps} < 3.99 for every k ≤ 29 and every 0 ≤ eps < 1, so the enlarged simplex alone cannot give DHL[k,2] for k ≤ 29 from Bombieri-Vinogradov or any level θ ≤ 0.501. Inequality proved; numerical part Computed in interval arithmetic and re-checked with a second library.

results.label: Computed
results.text: M_55 ≥ 4.00516 with even power sums of degree 20 (707 coefficients). With the Lean tuple (55, 272), Bombieri-Vinogradov and Maynard's Prop. 4.2 this gives H1 ≤ 272 end to end. Reproduction, not new; M_54 at degree 23 (for 270) was still running.

results.text: The twin prime conjecture is equivalent to BoundedGaps 2.

results.label: Lean-checked
results.text: A finite Boolean check certifies admissibility (pigeonhole handles large primes).

results.label: Lean-checked
results.text: DHL[k,2] implies gaps at most D for 56 explicit pairs (k, D): every k from 2 to 55, plus (102, 578) and (105, 600). DHL[2,2] implies the twin prime conjecture.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Pigeonhole rigidity: unequal weights on the shifts never certify a smaller gap than the best sub-tuple does (Proposition 5). Possibly folklore.

results.label: Computed
results.text: With polynomials in 1-P1 and P2 only: M_105 ≥ 4.00207, M_102 ≥ 4.00271, M_5 ≥ 2.00411. This family stops at k = 102.

results.label: Computed
results.text: With all symmetric polynomials (new generating-function formula): M_105 ≥ 4.17427, M_64 ≥ 4.00363 (degree 12); even power sums: M_58 ≥ 4.00927 (degree 16), M_56 ≥ 4.00519 (degree 18). M_55 reaches only 3.99153 at degree 18.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Exponential-moment formula: integrals of (1-P1)^A times products of power sums over the simplex are A!/(k+A+w)! times E[prod P_j(X)^b_j] for iid Exp(1) variables, an integer given by an EGF power (Lemma 3). Possibly folklore.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Pigeonhole rigidity also holds on Polymath8b's epsilon-enlarged simplex (Proposition 8): weights never beat the best sub-tuple. Possibly folklore.

results.label: Literature
results.text: With Bombieri-Vinogradov and Maynard's Prop. 4.2, the M_55 certificate and the Lean tuple (55, 272) give H1 ≤ 272 end to end inside this project (was 278).

ideas.idea: Active-count-normalised weight (beta/n)(a − S_A + n t_m) to beat scaling at small eps.
ideas.note: Exact fiber evaluation at k = 50, eps = 1/25: never below 4.178, worse than the scaling bound 4.1515 (Remark 16).

ideas.idea: Two-zone dual weight (linear in t_m below s1, proportional to t_m/S above) in Polymath8b's Lemma 6.1 with the marginal region kept, to bound M_{k,eps} uniformly in eps.
ideas.note: Theorem 13: no k ≤ 29 for any eps < 1, beating the k ≤ 23 floor from Polymath8b Prop. 6.5.

ideas.idea: Exponential-moment generating function for simplex integrals of power-sum products, to make certified high-degree computations cheap.
ideas.note: Lemma 3. Builds a 471x471 exact Gram pair in about 15 s.

ideas.idea: Weighted pigeonhole: give the shifts unequal weights to force two primes closer than the tuple's diameter.
ideas.note: Convexity plus perfection of unit interval graphs. Proved as Proposition 5; checked numerically for k = 3.

ideas.idea: Floor of the method: a rigorous upper bound (dual certificate) for the 2026 hybrid sieve supports, to learn how far below 186 the present inputs can go.
ideas.note: Done for the eps-enlarged simplex down to k ≤ 29 (Theorem 13). The true threshold is near k = 50; Remark 16 records a weight that fails (4.178 vs 4.1515). Hybrid 2026 supports still open.

ideas.idea: Does the slicing lemma behind Proposition 5 survive on enlarged supports?
ideas.note: Yes: a single rescaling by (1+eps-|u|)/(1+eps) keeps each slice inside the eps-problem's J-region. Proposition 8; checked numerically for k = 3 and eps up to 1/3.

ideas.idea: Richer symmetric test functions to pass k = 102 and reach M_54 > 4 (270).
ideas.note: M_55 ≥ 4.00516 at degree 20 (272). M_54 needs degree 23 (Polymath8b): over 15 min and 9 GB here.

ideas.idea: One explicit bilinear hypothesis that implies twin primes, formalised in Lean.
ideas.note: Track B. Start from Bombieri's asymptotic sieve and Heath-Brown's Siegel-zero theorem.
